item.title: জুলাইয়ের ধাক্কা সামলে আগস্টে যুক্তরাজ্যে পোশাক রফতানি বাড়লো
item.description:
যুক্তরাজ্যের বাজারে বাংলাদেশের তৈরি পোশাক রফতানিতে নতুন অর্থবছরের শুরুটা দুর্বল হলেও আগস্টে তা ঘুরে দাঁড়িয়েছে। জুলাইয়ে রফতানি কমলেও আগস্টে ১০ দশমিক ৫৩ শতাংশ প্রবৃদ্ধি হয়েছে। ফলে ২০২৬-২৭ অর্থবছরের প্রথম দুই মাসে যুক্তরাজ্যে বাংলাদেশের তৈরি পোশাক রফতানি আগের বছরের একই সময়ের তুলনায় ৩ দশমিক ৭৪ শতাংশ বেড়েছে।
রফতানি উন্নয়ন ব্যুরোর (ইপিবি) তথ্য অনুযায়ী, চলতি অর্থবছরের জুলাই ও আগস্টে যুক্তরাজ্যে ৯১ কোটি ৫৬ লাখ ৩০ হাজার মার্কিন ডলারের তৈরি পোশাক রফতানি হয়েছে। আগের অর্থবছরের একই সময়ে রফতানি হয়েছিল ৮৮ কোটি ২৬ লাখ ২০ হাজার ডলার। অর্থাৎ দুই মাসে রফতানি বেড়েছে ৩ কোটি ৩০ লাখ ১০ হাজার ডলার।
জুলাইয়ে কমেছিল, আগস্টে বেড়েছে
ইপিবির তথ্য বলছে, চলতি অর্থবছরের জুলাইয়ে যুক্তরাজ্যে তৈরি পোশাক রফতানি আগের বছরের একই মাসের তুলনায় ২ দশমিক ৪৪ শতাংশ কমে যায়। তবে আগস্টে রফতানি বেড়েছে ১০ দশমিক ৫৩ শতাংশ।
আগস্টের এই প্রবৃদ্ধির ফলে জুলাইয়ের নেতিবাচক প্রবৃদ্ধি পুষিয়ে দুই মাসের সম্মিলিত রফতানি ইতিবাচক ধারায় ফিরেছে।
দুই মাসের গড়ও বেশি
চলতি অর্থবছরের প্রথম দুই মাসে যুক্তরাজ্যে বাংলাদেশের তৈরি পোশাক রফতানির মাসিক গড় দাঁড়িয়েছে ৪৫ কোটি ৭৮ লাখ ২০ হাজার ডলার।
অন্যদিকে, ২০২৫-২৬ অর্থবছরে যুক্তরাজ্যে বাংলাদেশের তৈরি পোশাক রফতানি হয়েছিল ৪৩৮ কোটি ৮৫ লাখ ৫০ হাজার ডলার। সে হিসাবে গত অর্থবছরে মাসিক গড় রফতানি ছিল প্রায় ৩৬ কোটি ৫৭ লাখ ডলার।
অর্থাৎ চলতি অর্থবছরের প্রথম দুই মাসে মাসিক গড় রফতানি গত অর্থবছরের মাসিক গড়ের চেয়ে বেশি। তবে মাত্র দুই মাসের তথ্য দিয়ে পুরো বছরের প্রবণতা নির্ধারণের সুযোগ নেই।
দুই মাসেই গত বছরের মোট রফতানির ২০.৮৬ শতাংশ
চলতি অর্থবছরের প্রথম দুই মাসের রফতানি গত অর্থবছরের পুরো বছরের রফতানির প্রায় এক-পঞ্চমাংশের সমান।
২০২৫-২৬ অর্থবছরে যুক্তরাজ্যে বাংলাদেশের মোট তৈরি পোশাক রফতানি ছিল ৪৩৮ কোটি ৮৫ লাখ ৫০ হাজার ডলার। এর বিপরীতে চলতি অর্থবছরের জুলাই-আগস্টে রফতানি হয়েছে ৯১ কোটি ৫৬ লাখ ৩০ হাজার ডলার। অর্থাৎ গত অর্থবছরের পুরো বছরের রফতানির ২০ দশমিক ৮৬ শতাংশ ইতোমধ্যে প্রথম দুই মাসে হয়েছে।
তবে পোশাক রফতানিতে মাসভেদে চাহিদা, ক্রয়াদেশ, উৎপাদন সক্ষমতা ও বাজার পরিস্থিতির প্রভাব থাকে। ফলে পরবর্তী মাসগুলোতে এই গতি ধরে রাখা যাবে কি না, সেটিই এখন গুরুত্বপূর্ণ।
‘যুক্তরাজ্যের বাজারে অবস্থান এখনও শক্ত’
বাংলাদেশ অ্যাপারেল ভয়েসের প্রতিষ্ঠাতা ও প্রধান নির্বাহী কর্মকর্তা মহিউদ্দিন রুবেল বাংলা ট্রিবিউনকে বলেন, জুলাইয়ে কিছুটা দুর্বলতার পর আগস্টে যুক্তরাজ্যে বাংলাদেশের পোশাক রফতানি ভালোভাবে ঘুরে দাঁড়িয়েছে। দুই মাসের সম্মিলিত হিসাবও ইতিবাচক প্রবৃদ্ধির ইঙ্গিত দিচ্ছে।
তিনি বলেন, মাসভিত্তিক ওঠানামার চেয়ে সামগ্রিক প্রবণতা দেখা গুরুত্বপূর্ণ। প্রথম দুই মাসের তথ্য বলছে, যুক্তরাজ্যের বাজারে বাংলাদেশের পোশাকের অবস্থান এখনো শক্ত রয়েছে। তবে এই প্রবৃদ্ধি ধরে রাখতে আন্তর্জাতিক বাজারের চাহিদা, ক্রেতাদের ক্রয়াদেশ এবং দেশের উৎপাদন সক্ষমতার বিষয়গুলো গুরুত্ব দিতে হবে।
সামনে চ্যালেঞ্জ
যুক্তরাজ্যে পোশাক রফতানি বাড়লেও আন্তর্জাতিক বাজারে প্রতিযোগিতা রয়েছে। ক্রেতাদের মূল্যসংবেদনশীলতা, উৎপাদন ব্যয়, জ্বালানি ও পরিবহন খরচ এবং বৈশ্বিক অর্থনীতির গতি রফতানির ওপর প্রভাব ফেলছে।
এ কারণে একটি মাসের প্রবৃদ্ধি দিয়ে পুরো বছরের বাজার পরিস্থিতি বিচার করার সুযোগ নেই। আগামী কয়েক মাসে রফতানির ধারাবাহিকতা বজায় থাকে কি না, সেটিই হবে মূল বিষয়।
তবে অর্থবছরের প্রথম দুই মাসে ৩ দশমিক ৭৪ শতাংশ প্রবৃদ্ধি এবং আগস্টে ১০ দশমিক ৫৩ শতাংশ রফতানি বৃদ্ধি জুলাইয়ের দুর্বলতার পর যুক্তরাজ্যের বাজারে বাংলাদেশের পোশাক রফতানিতে গতি ফেরার ইঙ্গিত দিচ্ছে।

item.title: Bangladesh, Turkiye discuss PM's participation in COP31
item.description:
Bangladesh and Turkiye have discussed the possible participation of Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in COP31, to be hosted by Turkiye in Antalya.
The discussion took place when State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir met Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Friday on the sidelines of the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly, according to a Foreign Ministry press release.
During the meeting, they exchanged views on the upcoming climate summit, including the prime minister's possible participation. However, the press release did not mention any decision on this.
The two sides also discussed high-level visits, defence cooperation, renewable and green energy and investment opportunities for Turkish companies in Bangladesh.
Kobir invited Turkiye to participate in an international sports conference that Bangladesh plans to host in early 2027.
Both sides expressed their commitment to further strengthening cooperation in areas of mutual interest.

item.description:
Bangladesh and the United States have signed a strategic civilian nuclear cooperation agreement aimed at the peaceful use of civilian nuclear energy.

Rehan Asad, prime minister’s adviser on science and technology, signed the agreement on behalf of Bangladesh, while US Under Secretary for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg signed on behalf of the United States.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP)’s media cell announced this on its verified Facebook page on Saturday.

According to diplomatic sources, the agreement was signed as part of a continuation of the nuclear cooperation initiative that began in 1981 during the rule of President Ziaur Rahman.

The agreement will increase technical exchanges, nuclear safety and scientific cooperation in the civilian energy sector between Dhaka and Washington.

item.title: Cabinet clears draft VAT law requiring returns within 15 days
item.description:
The Cabinet on Monday gave the final approval, subject to vetting by the Legislative and Parliamentary Affairs Division, to a draft ordinance seeking to restore the provision requiring taxpayers to submit VAT returns within 15 days after the end of each tax period instead of every three tax periods.
The clearance was given to the draft Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 2026 at the cabinet meeting held with Prime Minister Tarique Rahman in the chair at the Bangladesh Secretariat.
The draft law proposed amendment to section 64 of the Value Added Tax and Supplementary Duty Act, 2012, to bring greater dynamism to revenue collection at the field level.
Under the proposed provision, VAT returns will have to be submitted within 15 days of the end of each tax period, instead of the existing provision allowing submission within 15 days after the end of every three tax periods.
If the 15th day falls on a public holiday, the return may be submitted on the next working day.
The proposed amendment also provides additional time for certain taxpayers. Government, semi-government and autonomous bodies, banks, insurance companies, and individuals or entities submitting zero returns will be allowed to submit their returns within 20 days of the end of every tax period.
The Internal Resources Division placed the draft ordinance before the cabinet for both approval in-principle and final approval.

item.title: BB issues guidelines for dispute resolution in Bangla QR
item.description:
To make digital transactions safer, more transparent, and more customer-friendly, Bangladesh Bank has issued new guidelines for resolving disputes in Bangla QR (merchant payment) transactions.
The Payment Systems Department of the central bank issued a circular in this regard yesterday.
The guidelines will take effect on December 1.
According to the "Guidelines on Dispute Resolution for Bangla QR (Merchant Payment) Transactions," customers will not need to lodge a separate complaint for failed transactions. Once the system confirms a transaction failure, the money will be refunded automatically. If an immediate refund is not possible, it must be completed within a maximum of 30 minutes.
General disputes between customers and merchants using the same bank or MFS (Mobile Financial Services) provider must be resolved within three working days.
Meanwhile, transaction disputes involving different institutions will be settled through the NPSB's central Dispute Management System.
Customers can lodge complaints within 45 days of the transaction.
The issuing institution must communicate its decision within two working days.
The entire dispute resolution process, including chargebacks and arbitration if necessary, must be completed within a maximum of 30 days.
Additionally, in cases of QR code tampering, fraud, or unauthorized transactions, investigations must be completed within 30 days, and necessary refunds or compensation must be arranged.
Bangladesh Bank will take action under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2024 for non-compliance with these directions.

item.title: BB permits purchase of foreign airline tickets via credit cards
item.description:
Bangladesh Bank has allowed passengers to purchase tickets for foreign airlines operating in Bangladesh directly using international credit and debit cards.
As a result, in addition to traditional banking channels or travel agencies, passengers will now be able to pay for tickets directly using international cards.
On Monday (September 28), the Foreign Exchange Policy Department (FEPD-1) of Bangladesh Bank issued a circular in this regard and sent it to all authorized dealer (AD) banks.
The circular states that, subject to holding a valid visa, Bangladeshi citizens can use international cards to purchase tickets for foreign airlines operating in the country for overseas travel.
This facility will also apply to foreign airlines whose ticket sales proceeds are settled outside Bangladesh through international acquiring and payment settlement systems.
According to Bangladesh Bank instructions, this card-based ticket purchasing facility will remain outside the prescribed annual travel quota.
However, after verifying the authenticity of the ticket purchase, the respective bank can refill or adjust the funds used on the customer's card.
Banks must follow the specific Merchant Category Code (MCC) of the respective airline to identify such transactions.
However, this facility for purchasing tickets through foreign platforms will not apply to domestic airlines of Bangladesh.
That is, if a ticket for a Bangladeshi airline is purchased through a platform providing services from outside the country, this facility will not be available.
The circular further states that foreign currency earned from ticket sales must be calculated and adjusted as remittable surplus according to existing guidelines when remitting it to the airline's home country.
Additionally, information on these transactions must be regularly reported through Bangladesh Bank's TM (Transaction Monitoring) module.
The circular, signed by Md Abu Bakkarr Siddique, director of Bangladesh Bank (FEPD-1), has been ordered to take effect immediately.

item.title: Govt drafts market-specific export strategies for 18 key destinations
item.description:
The government is preparing an integrated strategy to diversify both products and markets, aiming to boost export earnings and reduce the country's heavy dependence on ready-made garments (RMG).
Under the initiative, separate market-based export strategies are being drafted for 18 key trading destinations worldwide, based on an analysis of market potential, existing barriers, competitors' positions and the steps Bangladesh needs to take.
Commerce secretary Ataur Rahman Khan announced the move while presiding over a workshop titled "Bangladesh Export Diversification Strategy: Product and Market Diversification Across 18 Key Trading Destinations" at the Secretariat on Monday.
"Equal importance is being given to both product diversification and market diversification to make Bangladesh's exports stronger and more sustainable," he said.
He said detailed country profiles and implementable strategies are being prepared after collecting and analyzing information on the 18 selected destinations.
Information on the current situation in the target markets, existing export barriers, Bangladesh's potential products and scope for trade expansion has been gathered from the country's commercial wings abroad, the secretary said. "A separate action plan will be drawn up for each country by consolidating this data."
Ataur said a specific matrix is being followed for market analysis. "It includes Bangladesh's share in the country's total imports, main competitors for specific products, ways to enhance competitiveness, and the policy and institutional measures needed for market expansion."
He added that the analysis of the 18 markets would help identify new potential products, expand markets for existing items and determine the steps required to enter new markets.
Speaking at the workshop, Mustafizur Rahman, Distinguished Fellow of the Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), said services exports must receive equal priority alongside goods in any diversification drive.
He called for effective initiatives to develop information technology, the skills-based economy and enabling service sectors, along with support for the growth of freelancers.
Stressing skills development and technological upgrading, he said greater use of technology in manufacturing and services is essential to improve competitiveness in international markets.
He also suggested stepping up efforts to increase exports of Bangladeshi goods and services to neighbouring countries by leveraging geographical proximity.
Representatives of the BGMEA, Flexa, CPD, Walton Group, Bangladesh Agro-Processors' Association and the pharmaceutical sector, among others, placed their proposals for expanding exports at the workshop.
Officials from the Ministry of Commerce and other relevant ministries and organizations also attended.
Participants emphasized making sectors such as pharmaceuticals, electronics, agriculture and agro-processed products, leather and leather goods, light engineering, information technology and other services more competitive in global markets, alongside RMG.
Stakeholders said the strategy centred on the 18 destinations would play a key role in broadening the export base, creating new products and markets, deepening partnerships in existing markets and building a diversified, sustainable export structure in the long run.

item.title: Banglalink brings mobile services to ChatGPT
item.description:
Banglalink has brought its core mobile services into ChatGPT in the first such integration by a telecom operator in Bangladesh, allowing customers to access everyday mobile services through a simple conversation, reports a press release.

With Banglalink GPT, subscribers can manage everyday telco needs directly through ChatGPT, from checking their balance and usage and finding suitable packs to checking roaming status and accessing other key mobile services, without having to switch between different apps or websites.

Developed by Banglalink Digital, the service is now live nationwide for Banglalink subscribers. They can find Banglalink GPT in ChatGPT’s GPT section and use it by simply asking questions in everyday language.

Banglalink GPT also recommends suitable packs to users based on their needs and usage. For instance, a customer planning to watch a movie can ask which pack would be suitable, while another can ask to check their current balance, minutes or internet data.

Customers can also check their roaming status through the assistant. For services that require a transaction, customers can complete the process through Banglalink’s payment portal.

Taimur Rahman, chief corporate & regulatory affairs Officer of Banglalink, said, “Customer expectations are evolving rapidly as AI becomes increasingly integrated into everyday life. At Banglalink, we believe that accessing and managing mobile services should evolve accordingly. By becoming the first telecom operator in Bangladesh to bring our services into ChatGPT, we are making it easier for customers to discover, manage, and purchase the services they need through a familiar conversational interface. This initiative reflects our commitment to using technology to make digital experiences more intuitive, accessible, and customer-centric”

The new service is part of Banglalink’s broader effort as a digital operator to make everyday services simpler and more accessible through technology.

item.title: Bangladesh wants to join trade bloc RCEP, what could it gain
item.description:
Bangladesh’s bid to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP), one of the world’s largest free trade blocs, has moved a step forward. Trade ministers from the bloc’s member countries have approved a recommendation to form a special task force to advance formal discussions and technical procedure involving Bangladesh and three other applicant countries.

Alongside Bangladesh, Chile, Sri Lanka and Hong Kong have applied to join the 15-country trade bloc in the Asia-Pacific region. At a meeting of the RCEP Joint Committee in Manila on 21 September, a recommendation was made to form a special task force for the applicant countries. The recommendation was later approved at the fifth RCEP Ministerial Meeting, also held in the Philippine capital, Manila.

RCEP is a bloc comprising 15 countries, including China, Japan and South Korea. Trade among its member countries was worth around USD 2.1 trillion. Becoming an RCEP member could create opportunities for Bangladesh to receive preferential trade benefits in the markets of member countries.

Efforts are underway to sign as many trade agreements as possible before LDC graduation

It would also cover areas such as services, investment, intellectual property, e-commerce, competition, dispute settlement and support for small and medium-sized enterprises.

Bangladesh began initial efforts and discussions to join RCEP in 2022. Two months after the interim government led by Professor Muhammad Yunus took office, it sent a letter in October 2024 expressing its interest. RCEP at the time however, had not yet decided on admitting new members.

In 2025, RCEP members approved a process for admitting new countries. Bangladesh, Sri Lanka, Chile and Hong Kong subsequently submitted formal applications. As part of the formal application process for joining RCEP, Bangladesh has already submitted the required documents.

At a joint press conference with the prime minister of Malaysia last June, Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman said Bangladesh was interested in joining RCEP and welcomed Malaysia’s support on the matter. Bangladesh has also sought Australia’s support in this regard.

Sources at the Ministry of Commerce said the task force will work to advance formal discussions and the technical process with Bangladesh and the other interested countries, in line with the roadmap for expanding the bloc and admitting new members.

Commerce Secretary Md Ataur Rahman Khan told Prothom Alo, “We want to become a member of RCEP. The good news is that at the RCEP Joint Committee meeting last Monday, we received a positive indication regarding membership for all four countries, including Bangladesh. As Bangladesh’s process of graduating from the least developed country (LDC) category moves forward, we will benefit if we can become a member of the bloc.”

Experts say joining RCEP is important for Bangladesh mainly because of the opportunities it could create for tariff benefits in export markets and trade expansion. After graduating from the LDC category, Bangladesh may lose tariff benefits in various countries.

Becoming an RCEP member could create opportunities to receive preferential trade benefits in the markets of bloc members. Alongside benefits in goods trade, the agreement would also cover services, investment, intellectual property, e-commerce, competition, dispute settlement and support for small and medium-sized enterprises.

Bangladesh hopeful of signing FTA with Malaysia by 2027

Bangladesh will gain tariff benefits, but must offer them too

Officials at the Ministry of Commerce say Bangladesh joining RCEP could play an important role in addressing the challenges following graduation from the LDC category, retaining tariff benefits in international trade, strengthening links with global supply chains and attracting foreign direct investment to the country.

Who are RCEP’s members, and how much they trade

RCEP currently comprises the 10 members of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN): Brunei, Cambodia, Indonesia, Laos, Malaysia, Myanmar, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam. There are five other countries: China, Japan, South Korea, Australia and New Zealand.

The bloc represents around 30 per cent of global gross domestic product (GDP) and population. In 2024, trade among its member countries was worth around USD 2.1 trillion.

According to a report by the Bangladesh Trade and Tariff Commission, RCEP countries account for 53.90 per cent of Bangladesh’s total imports and 7.92 per cent of its exports. In other words, becoming a member of the bloc could create an opportunity for Bangladesh to further institutionalise its trade relations with major import and export markets.

‘Bangladesh will have to negotiate skilfully’

It is learnt that Bangladesh would need the consent of all 15 existing RCEP members to join the bloc. It would also have to demonstrate its ability to comply with the agreement’s rules and regulations and offer market access to member countries.

Bangladesh’s main tasks now, therefore, are to negotiate its membership, make proposals on market access and bargain over various terms of the agreement. Key issues include how much tariff preference will be granted on which products, how quickly those preferences will be implemented and what kind of market access Bangladesh will have to offer.

How new US tariff will affect Bangladesh’s trade

The Manila meeting reportedly emphasised strengthening regional economic integration through cooperation and constructive dialogue among member countries. It also stressed the need to remove unnecessary barriers to international trade and to put emphasis on the World Trade Organization (WTO) reform process.

Mustafizur Rahman, distinguished fellow at the private research organisation Centre for Policy Dialogue (CPD), told Prothom Alo that after graduating from the LDC category, Bangladesh would need to pursue free trade agreements (FTAs) and comprehensive economic partnership agreements (CEPAs) with various countries. From that perspective, joining a trade bloc such as RCEP would be beneficial for Bangladesh.

“Bangladesh has initiatives under way to sign FTAs with some countries. At the same time, among RCEP members there are some strong economies as well as some weaker ones. Alongside receiving trade benefits, members also have to provide benefits to other member countries. That is the main challenge. Bangladesh will have to negotiate skilfully to address this challenge. I would like to have confidence that Bangladesh will do so,” he added.

Gold prices drop further
item.description:
The Bangladesh Jewellers Association (Bajus) has reduced gold prices again, with the price of 22-carat gold falling by Tk185 per gram.
Under the new rates, 22-carat hallmarked gold will cost Tk19,785 per gram, including VAT.
The new prices came into effect at 10am on Monday, following another reduction announced by Bajus on Saturday.
The Bajus Standing Committee on Pricing and Price Monitoring set the new rates at a meeting at 9am on Monday. The decision was announced in a notification signed by the committee’s chairman, Dr Dewan Aminul Islam Shahin.
The price of one bhori (11.664 grams) of 22-carat gold now stands at approximately Tk230,770, including VAT. Making charges will be added separately depending on the design of the jewellery.
The price of 21-carat gold has been set at Tk18,895 per gram, while 18-carat gold will cost Tk16,225 per gram. Gold sold under the traditional method has been priced at Tk13,225 per gram.
On September 26, the price of 22-carat gold stood at Tk19,970 per gram, including VAT. The price per bhori was reduced by Tk1,691 that day.
With Monday’s reduction, the price of 22-carat gold has fallen by approximately Tk2,159 per bhori over two days.
Bajus has also reduced the prices of silver jewellery.
Under the new rates, 22-carat silver will cost Tk385 per gram, 21-carat silver Tk370, 18-carat silver Tk320 and traditional-method silver Tk240 per gram.
The price of 22-carat silver was Tk415 per gram on September 26, meaning it has fallen by Tk30 per gram in two days.
Bajus said making charges will be applicable separately based on the design of the jewellery.
However, as VAT is already included in the fixed selling price, it cannot be charged separately from customers.
For exchanges involving old gold jewellery, 12% will be deducted from the gold price, excluding making charges and the cost of stones. For purchases of old jewellery, the deduction will be 18%.
VAT cannot be deducted separately in either exchange or purchase transactions, according to Bajus.
The new rates will remain in effect at jewellery shops across the country until further notice.
Bajus said the decision was taken after reviewing the overall market situation, including a decline in the prices of raw gold and silver.

item.title: Bangladesh is open for business, PM Tarique Rahman tells Wall Street firms
item.description:
Prime Minister Tarique Rahman on Friday invited Wall Street firms to invest in Bangladesh, saying the country is “open for business” and ready to serve as a strong platform for investors seeking access to the wider regional market.

“We welcome Wall Street firms to invest in Bangladesh. And we want Bangladesh to become a strong platform, from which you can serve a much larger regional market,” he said.

“Our message is simple: Bangladesh is open for business,” the Prime Minister said while addressing a breakfast meeting with business leaders and investors hosted by JPMorgan Chase at its headquarters in Manhattan.

Tarique Rahman said his government was determined to create “confidence, predictability and the right conditions to grow” for investors, stressing that investment needs a conducive and predictable business environment.

“Before entering politics, I started my career in business. I learned a simple lesson: investment needs confidence, predictability and the right conditions to grow,” he said.

The Prime Minister said Bangladesh, with a population of more than 180 million, has a young and hardworking population, a growing market and a strategic location.

He said Bangladesh was known globally as a major manufacturing and garments base, but the country now offered significant opportunities in energy, infrastructure, logistics, technology, digital services, climate finance, manufacturing, agriculture and healthcare.

“Our ambition is to build a one-trillion-dollar economy by 2034 and position Bangladesh as a globally connected manufacturing, investment and services hub,” he said.

The Prime Minister said the government was working to make Bangladesh “easier and more predictable” for investors through deregulation, stronger investor protection, easier regulations, improved tax and VAT administration, easier profit repatriation and better infrastructure.

He also highlighted Bangladesh’s efforts to deepen economic ties with major global economies, saying the country had signed a Reciprocal Trade Agreement with the United States, reached new economic arrangements with Japan and South Korea, initiated a new partnership with the European Union and strengthened economic ties with China.

“These are important steps in connecting Bangladesh more closely with the world’s major economies,” he said.

Referring to JPMorgan’s role in Bangladesh’s inaugural sovereign bond, the Prime Minister described it as an important milestone that gave international investors a new reference point for Bangladesh and helped connect the country’s capital markets more closely with the global financial system.

Tarique Rahman said investors wanted to know whether regulations were predictable, investments were protected, capital could move efficiently and profits could be repatriated, describing these as “legitimate questions”.

“Our responsibility is to provide confidence through policy and, most importantly, through implementation,” he said, adding that Bangladesh was seeking long-term partnerships rather than short-term transactions.

“Our government’s objective is straightforward. More investment. More trade. More jobs. More technology. And a stronger economic partnership between Bangladesh and the United States,” he said.

The Prime Minister invited the investors to build long-term partnerships with Bangladesh.

“I invite you to invest with confidence and build for the long term. We are ready to work with you, listen to you and remove obstacles where we can. I hope we will see many of you soon in Bangladesh,” he said.

The breakfast meeting was held as part of the Prime Minister’s engagements in New York during his visit to attend the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly.
